selectedCourses.name: Personal & Professional Development
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
selectedCourses.contribution: First-year academic writing,research literacy,personal development and civic engagement.

selectedCourses.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces financial accounting, management accounting and investment appraisal, including accounting's social role and accountability implications. Students record transactions, prepare and interpret financial statements, and analyze performance and financing. The course then examines costing, pricing, budgeting, organizational control and sustainable management accounting. Investment decisions are evaluated using accounting and discounted-cash-flow measures. A case study analyzes the misuse of an accounting principle and its financial-statement effects.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. Students learn how to comprehend a typical corporate annual report and to use accounting as a tool in understanding how economic events affect business.
selectedCourses.contribution: Develops financial and management accounting, financial-statement analysis, costing,budgeting and NPV/IRR investment appraisal; these are substantive accounting and corporate-finance tools.
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. selectedCourses.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. AI foundations and limitations lead into applications across enterprise functions and industries, labour-market change, productivity, innovation, market structure and inequality. Governance, corporate responsibility, regulation and future scenarios connect technological developments to institutional choices. Students analyze business cases and competing scholarly arguments, then investigate a country's AI readiness, workforce, regulation and industrial policy.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: This course includes a multi-faceted exploration of AI’s business, managerial, economic and related societal implications. Designed for students with a strong interest in AI, it requires no prior technical background.
selectedCourses.contribution: examines the economic and managerial consequences of AI and technological change
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. Students study AI's capabilities and limits, applications across business functions and industries, and effects on labour markets, productivity, innovation and inequality. selectedCourses.name: Money, Banking & Finance
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines financial markets and institutions, including the pricing of bonds, stocks and derivatives, interest rates and their risk and term structure, commercial-bank balance sheets and performance, financial structure and regulation, banking fragility and financial crises, central banks, money creation and monetary policy. Students apply algebraic and graphical analysis to financial and monetary problems. In the Stanford Banking Game they manage a simulated bank, analyse performance in Excel dashboards, forecast financial statements, and make evidence-based decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk. A small research project extends a selected financial or monetary research article through additional literature, a case study or updated evidence.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: We study financial markets (stocks, bonds, derivatives) and financial institutions (commercial banks and central banks). We address such questions as: Can you outperform the stock market? Why are banks inherently fragile? What do central banks do? What causes financial crises? Throughout the semester, student teams participate in a business simulation, the Stanford Banking Game. Each team manages a virtual bank and tries to maximize its share price.
selectedCourses.contribution: Studies bonds,stocks,derivatives,banking,risk and monetary institutions, with simulated bank management and a financial/monetary research project. It is not specialist stochastic finance.
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Examines financial markets, commercial banks and central banks, including interest rates, financial regulation, financial crises and monetary policy. Students analyse financial problems and manage a simulated bank in the Stanford Banking Game, using Excel dashboards and financial forecasts to inform decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk.

selectedCourses.name: Introduction to Economics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces microeconomic principles and short-run macroeconomic analysis. The microeconomic component examines supply and demand, strategic interaction, consumer choice, production, costs and competitive markets. The macroeconomic component introduces output, unemployment and inflation, then relates goods and financial markets through the IS-LM model. Students use algebra and graphs to explain economic behaviour and apply models to economic issues.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.
selectedCourses.contribution: provides foundational microeconomic and macroeconomic analysis of markets, firms, households and the wider economy
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.

selectedCourses.name: International Macroeconomics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines short-, medium- and long-run macroeconomic dynamics and policy, including international dimensions. Students study goods, financial and labour markets, inflation and unemployment, economic growth, expectations and the open economy. IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models connect markets and policy effects. Algebraic and graphical analysis and interpretation of macroeconomic indicators support the evaluation of economic developments and fiscal and monetary policy.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Study the economy as a whole through topics such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment. Understand how governments and central banks use fiscal and monetary policies to influence economic performance over time. The course also explores business cycles, international trade, and economic crises, preparing students to evaluate policy debates and global economic trends.
selectedCourses.contribution: examines growth, inflation, unemployment, finance, exchange rates and macroeconomic policy

selectedCourses.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Develops microeconomic theory through consumer behaviour, imperfectly competitive markets and economy-wide allocation. Students examine choice under uncertainty, non-egoistic preferences and cognitive limitations, then monopoly, strategic behaviour and labour and capital markets. General equilibrium, efficiency, externalities and government complete the analysis. Algebraic problem-solving and graphical analysis are connected to the interpretation and evaluation of research papers.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity. Explore key concepts such as rational choice, decision-making under uncertainty, and non-egoistic preferences. Analyze market structures, strategic interactions, and factor markets. Learn how markets function and examine the impact of regulation. Develop analytical tools to better understand behavior and engage with empirical research.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops advanced microeconomic analysis of choice under uncertainty, firms and markets

selectedCourses.name: Public Economics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines government intervention through the efficiency and equity effects of public policy. Market failure, public goods and externalities provide foundations for studying public production, collective choice, spending and taxation. Health, education, welfare and social insurance illustrate expenditure and redistribution questions. Students apply economic models, interpret data and graphs, evaluate research and develop a research proposal and paper.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.
selectedCourses.contribution: examines market failure, public goods, externalities, taxation, redistribution and government intervention
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. selectedCourses.name: Econometrics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.

selectedCourses.name: Consumer Product Design
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Teaches consumer-product design and development through projects that progress from understanding an existing product to creating a new one. Students investigate product mechanisms and environmental impact, interview potential customers, translate needs into specifications, select concepts, and develop production plans and prototypes where feasible. The final project integrates these stages with industrial scaling and elementary economic analysis. Sustainability, including material use, repairability, lifespan and circularity, informs design decisions throughout.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.

selectedCourses.name: International Business & Governance

Economic foundations include trade theories, foreign direct investment, foreign exchange and the monetary system. Students analyze governance, responsibility and trade-policy conflicts, investigate an international-business question, and develop an evidence-based market-entry strategy covering country attractiveness and business functions. A tariff case applies game theory to stakeholder choices and negotiation.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: This course examines the institutional, political and cultural forces shaping global businesses. It provides a comprehensive understanding of today’s complex international business environment.

selectedCourses.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces entrepreneurship and core business functions through the development of a startup concept. Students use design thinking to discover customer needs, define a problem, generate and prototype solutions, and construct value propositions and business models. Marketing, finance, operations, human resources and funding inform a coherent business plan and investor pitch. Entrepreneurial cases and a startup simulation examine decision-making, early growth and business lifecycles, with attention to societal impact and sustainability.

selectedCourses.name: Research Methods & Statistics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.

You’ll learn how to plan research logically, from designing studies to working with real data using experimental and survey techniques. You’ll also study descriptive and inferential statistics, with a brief intro to multivariate tools.

selectedCourses.name: Decision-making in AI

Decision theory, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems connect uncertainty to policies and expected utility. Multi-agent decisions introduce strategic and collective interaction, and probabilistic programming provides a framework for expressing models. Students work through equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Introduces planning techniques for AI systems in deterministic and non‑deterministic environments. Addresses uncertainty, partial observability, resource planning and optimizing behaviour under constraints.

selectedCourses.name: Ethics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Studies moral reasoning through historical and contemporary ethical theories and close philosophical reading. Utilitarianism, consequentialism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics lead into Nietzsche's genealogy, Murdoch's account of goodness and Nagel's treatments of value, perspective, death and meaning. Reflection and research essays require interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Explores theories of moral reasoning—virtue ethics, deontology, utilitarianism—and discusses moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure. Applies theories to practical issues such as animal rights, privacy, future generations, war, punishment, disability and equality.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops ethical reasoning for evaluating economic, business and public-policy choices
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Ethics examines moral reasoning through historical and contemporary theories and close philosophical reading. Students study utilitarianism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics, alongside Nietzsche, Murdoch and Nagel. Reflection and research essays develop interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.

selectedCourses.name: Social Psychology
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces the scientific study of how thoughts, feelings and behaviour are shaped by other people and social situations. Social cognition, the self, influence and persuasion lead into group processes, prejudice, aggression, prosocial behaviour, attraction and close relationships. Students critically examine empirical research, synthesize findings from journal articles, formulate theory-guided questions and design a feasible study. The final project proposes research rather than conducting an empirical investigation.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Covers main theories, findings and principles of social psychology, emphasising its scientific approach to understanding how people’s feelings, thoughts and behaviour are influenced by the presence of others.
selectedCourses.contribution: provides social-psychological analysis of attitudes, influence and group behaviour relevant to consumer and economic choices

selectedCourses.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Develops experimental-design knowledge and practical statistical analysis for health and behavioural research. Students choose, fit, diagnose and interpret multivariable models, comparing means, analyzing categorical outcomes and studying latent constructs. R, primarily through R Commander, supports repeated practical exercises; SPSS is an optional alternative. Data-analysis papers and a poster connect research questions and hypotheses to appropriate models, assumption checks, substantive interpretation and APA reporting.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: The course is necessary for students who want to pursue master programs in psychology and adjacent disciplines, as well as research masters in the medical domain. It is highly recommended also for all those who want to be researchers in other domains. In addition to technical training, the course emphasizes clear academic communication. It will equip you with the skills necessary to apply advanced statistical techniques to real-world research problems. With a focus on practical application through case studies and data analysis projects, You will be able to choose the appropriate statistical model for various research scenarios and address common challenges in data interpretation.
selectedCourses.contribution: provides multivariate statistics and experimental methods for studying human decision-making
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Develops experimental-design knowledge and practical statistical analysis for health and behavioural research. Students choose, fit, diagnose and interpret multivariable models for group comparisons, categorical outcomes and latent constructs. R, primarily through R Commander, supports practical exercises; data-analysis papers and a poster connect research questions to appropriate models, assumption checks and clear reporting.

selectedCourses.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Teaches rhetorical analysis and persuasive communication through classical history, theory and practice. Students study Greek and Roman rhetoric, the five canons, types of discourse, persuasive appeals, argumentation and fallacies. Written exercises, debates and public speeches develop invention, arrangement, style, memory and delivery. An applied project creates narrative and storytelling material for an immersive educational setting concerned with Zeeland's climate and community.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Teaches how to craft persuasive messages, influence opinions, inspire action and connect people. Draws on historical communicators from Aristotle to Barack Obama and applies stylistic techniques to students’ own writing and speaking.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops rhetorical analysis and persuasive communication relevant to advertising and consumer-facing messages
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: The Art of Rhetorical Communication develops rhetorical analysis, academic writing and oral presentation. Students examine classical Western roots and the canons of rhetoric, and learn to construct, organise and support persuasive arguments. Historical and contemporary examples connect rhetorical theory with practical communication.

selectedCourses.name: Persuasive Communication
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines contemporary persuasion through communication studies, social psychology and ethical analysis, then applies it in community-engaged work. Students study coactive persuasion, framing, argumentation, cognitive shortcuts and verbal and nonverbal communication. Projects with the Delta Climate Centre and Vlissingen municipality develop communication encouraging sustainable and circular lifestyles. An individual research paper evaluates selected persuasion tools through literature review, field research diaries and reflective analysis of their use.
selectedCourses.officialDescriptionRead: Explores ethical persuasion and climate communication. Students learn persuasive communication models and frameworks and collaborate with climate scientists at the Delta Climate Centre to produce sustainability messaging on water, food and energy.
selectedCourses.contribution: Studies persuasion,framing,nudging and ethics through actual sustainable/circular-lifestyle community projects, field diaries and research; no consumer-marketing assignment is assumed.

conceptJudgments: Closest materially addresses economic behaviour/markets,macro policy,business organisation,strategy,accounting,marketing and empirical analysis. Actual economics and business content organise the response,not generic skills. AI applications,business/organisation inquiry and introductory data/statistical methods are substantive bounded contributions. The fixed accounting,legal-taxation,history-of-thought and required major research sequences remain differences.

Behavioural/marketing direction adds actual behavioural economics,marketing/consumer engagement,market research,negotiation,leadership communication,social psychology and persuasion. Communication projects retain their actual climate/community and leadership subjects; they are not claimed to be consumer experiments. Five-course37.5EC difference replaces quantitative/finance/international context with behavioural and communication methods,not five unrelated companions.

Finance direction retains actual financial/management accounting and appraisal,banking/instrument pricing/monetary institutions,economics,econometrics,probability and advanced calculus. Software,data and mathematical decision models support quantitative reasoning without being specialist stochastic finance. Five-course37.5EC change from closest and ten-course75EC change from behavioural option are substantive.

All22generator interests723–744 reconciled with broad economics/business core or behavioural/marketing and financial candidates. Housing,energy and digitalisation are target applications of economic/business inquiry,not invented UCR field-specific syllabi or compulsory external specialisations. No fourth programme is generated from outcomes or individual theses. Three supported concepts meet the stopping rule,not a default quota.
alignmentFinding: Every external component and selected UCR identity assessed. Public Economics now occupies the actual public-economics part of Applied Microeconomics; the fiscal course includes tax-law structure and is left unmatched rather than using the same course twice. Microeconomics & Behavior provides the stronger microeconomic subject placement. Market Research does not become the cross-section economic causal-research project merely because both involve data collection. Intro accounting,strong empirical/regression,macroeconomic,marketing,mathematical and academic-writing partial relationships retained. Moral philosophy supplies only the normative foundation of welfare economics. Linear algebra supplies the matrix part of Mathematics and Game Theory; Nash theory and linear programming are not claimed. Finance supplies instruments/banking with corporate-valuation limits. Major courses,seminar,history,taxation,intermediate accounting,thesis and genuine choice retain meaningful gaps. Optional independent research15 remains additional/unscheduled.
alignments: Microeconomics & Behavior develops consumer choice,imperfect competition,strategic behaviour,general equilibrium and efficiency. It is a substantive partial relationship to the introductory microeconomics sequence.
Public Economics directly addresses the public-goods,externalities,intervention and distribution part. Personnel economics and worker incentive design remain differences.
The comparator contains a dedicated History of Economic Thought course. UCR does not add an unrelated history course merely to imitate this component.
Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations overlaps with organisation, markets and strategy but does not reproduce the comparator course in full.
Both study financial instruments and financial decisions. UCR emphasises banking,monetary institutions and risk; the comparator emphasises corporate valuation and investment/financing choices.
International Business & Governance overlaps with international economic and institutional environments but is broader and more business-governance oriented.
Research Methods & Statistics provides statistics and empirical research foundations, but is broader than Applied Statistics 1.
Linear Algebra directly covers matrix and vector methods in the comparator course, but not its full calculus, game-theory and linear-programming combination.

Ethics supplies utilitarian and other moral-theory foundations. It does not reproduce economic social-welfare functions,social-choice theory or the complete philosophical critique of welfare economics.
Personal & Professional Development overlaps with academic and professional formation but does not reproduce the comparator's economics-specific Academic Skills modules.
